guitar.evidence: The studio recording of Patience features three acoustic guitars playing together (Slash, Izzy, and Duff) with no electric guitars present. Slash used his Guild acoustic guitar for the solos and leads. All guitars are tuned down a half-step to Eb Standard.
guitar.notes: The original entry incorrectly assumed solid-body electric guitars (Les Paul, Telecaster) and electric clean amps were used on the track. This configuration adapts an electric guitar to simulate that pure acoustic texture, or optimizes the chain for an acoustic piezo pickup.
guitar.source: GGN'R Lies liner notes, interviews with Slash regarding acoustic tracking.

tone.target: Pure organic acoustic tone with warm compression and studio room ambience
tone.profile: Warm, bright, and highly dynamic acoustic guitar tone
tone.summary: To simulate or amplify the multi-layered acoustic vibe of Patience on the GP-180, we use a high-headroom clean amp (Silver Twin) set completely clean, paired with a compressor to smooth the picking dynamics and a parametric EQ to sculpt the acoustic 'air' while removing harsh electric mid-range.
mustHave: Acoustic guitar or acoustic simulator technique
Eb Standard Tuning (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb)
gearClues: No modulation on the original studio track
corrections: Removed Chorus and Delay blocks from active chain because the original track is dry acoustic rock, not an 80s chorused electric clean.
Changed amp to Silver Twin for maximum clean headroom and transparent reproduction.

rig.name: Guns N' Roses - Patience - Acoustic Simulation
rig.recommendedGuitar: Acoustic-Electric Guitar or Neck/Middle pickup on a Strat/Tele for clean acoustic simulation

blocks.purpose: Eliminate low-level single-coil hum or piezo hiss without cutting tails.
Evens out the dynamics of hard acoustic strumming and fingerpicking, mimicking studio compression.
Bypassed to maintain pristine clean tone.
Provides an ultra-clean, transparent platform with wide frequency response ideal for acoustic rendering.
blocks.gap: GP-180 lacks a dedicated acoustic preamp model; Silver Twin acts as a fallback.

alternatives.reason: Slightly warmer mid-range alternative if the Silver Twin sounds too bright.

blocks.purpose: Acts as a transparent speaker path to prevent harsh high frequencies from an electric guitar setup.
blocks.gap: Factory guitar cabinets impart an electric signature; an acoustic IR would be preferred.

alternatives.reason: Highly recommended to load a dedicated Acoustic Guitar IR here for true realism.

blocks.purpose: Scoops out boxy electric guitar mid-frequencies while boosting high-end brilliance to simulate acoustic string snap.
Bypassed (the studio track features purely organic acoustic tones without modulation effects).
Bypassed to maintain intimate and upfront acoustic presence.
Simulates a natural acoustic studio environment where the instruments were mic'd up.

improvements.summary: Implement a custom Acoustic Impulse Response for genuine acoustic tone realism.

proposals.recommendedAsset: Acoustic Guitar Body IR (e.g., Martin D-28 or Taylor 314 IR)
proposals.reason: A standard 2x12 electric guitar cabinet cannot faithfully replicate the wood resonance of an acoustic guitar body. Replacing the CAB block with a dedicated acoustic IR completely transforms an electric signal into a convincing acoustic tone.
proposals.whenToUse: Immediately to bypass electric cab coloration.
proposals.expectedGain: Elimination of synthetic high-end and introduction of rich wooden body resonance.
